about.heading: Developer by Curiosity. Creator by Passion.

about.bioParagraph1:
My journey into technology started much earlier than I ever imagined. Back in school, I wasn't just interested in playing Minecraft—I wanted to understand how it worked. I began experimenting with {bold & highlight}Minecraft Mods{bold & highlight}, texture packs, and small game modifications. Without realizing it, those small experiments became my first introduction to programming and problem-solving.

As my curiosity grew, I started learning programming languages like C, Java, Python, and JavaScript. What began as simple experiments slowly transformed into a passion for building real applications. Discovering web development introduced me to React, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and MySQL, allowing me to create complete full-stack applications that people could actually use. For me, development isn't just about writing code—it's about solving problems and turning ideas into reality through technology.

One of the projects I'm most proud of is my {bold & highlight}GFG Hackathon Project{bold & highlight}, where my team built an AI-powered SQL Query Generator capable of converting natural language prompts into SQL queries. That experience showed me how artificial intelligence can simplify complex tasks and inspired me to explore AI-powered development tools even further.

Alongside development, creativity became another important part of my journey. I enjoy designing {bold & highlight}posters{bold & highlight}, editing photos, producing videos, creating{bold & highlight} social media content{bold & highlight}, and experimenting with AI-assisted creative workflows. What started as a hobby gradually became another way for me to communicate ideas visually. Whether I'm designing an event poster or editing a promotional reel, I approach every creative project with the same attention to detail that I bring to software development.

Outside academics, I actively participate in {bold & highlight}NSS (National Service Scheme){bold & highlight} activities at my college. Joining NSS wasn't only about volunteering—it was also an opportunity to improve my digital skills, contribute to college events, build meaningful connections, and work toward becoming part of the college's creative and digital media team. It has helped me grow not only technically but also as a collaborator and communicator.

Alongside my personal learning journey, I actively seek opportunities to grow beyond the classroom. As an {bold & highlight}IEEE Student Member{bold & highlight}, I've been involved in activities that strengthen both my technical knowledge and professional network. I also contributed to organizing {bold & highlight}Vision Genix{bold & highlight}, a college-level AI Video Generation Competition, where I helped bring together creativity and emerging AI technologies. In addition, participating in hackathons has given me valuable experience in teamwork, problem-solving, and building practical solutions under time constraints. These experiences have taught me that learning isn't limited to courses—it's also about collaborating with people, taking initiative, and creating opportunities for yourself and others.

Beyond coding and design, gaming has always been one of my favorite hobbies. Having my own setup gives me a space to relax, explore new ideas, and stay inspired by the technology behind modern games. Many of those experiences continue to influence the way I think about software, user experience, and interactive design.
about.quote: I don't believe great developers are defined by the number of technologies they know—they're defined by their curiosity to keep learning. My journey began with modifying Minecraft, evolved into building full-stack web applications, and expanded into creative design through posters, photo editing, and video production.
about.quoteHighlight: Curiosity has always been my biggest motivation, and I believe it always will be.
about.philosophyParagraph1:
For me, learning never has a finish line. Every framework, every bug, every failed attempt, and every successful project adds another layer to my understanding. I believe the best way to master any skill is by building real projects, experimenting with new ideas, and never being afraid to start something challenging.

I'm especially fascinated by the future of {bold & highlight}Artificial Intelligence{bold & highlight} and developer tools. One of my long-term goals is to build my own {bold & highlight}Local AI Coding Agent{bold & highlight}—a free, privacy-focused assistant that runs locally and helps developers write code using open-source AI models. I want to create tools that make technology more accessible without requiring expensive subscriptions or cloud-based services.

My philosophy is simple: stay curious, keep building, and never stop improving. I don't aim to know everything—I aim to become a little better with every project I complete. Every website, every design, every line of code, and every challenge is another opportunity to learn, create, and move one step closer to becoming the developer and creator I aspire to be.

projects.title: INTELLI-Query
projects.summary: A conversational BI web application that lets users upload CSV files, ask questions in plain English, and receive instant {bold & highlight}AI-generated SQL queries{bold & highlight}, interactive charts, and data insights.
projects.description: A conversational BI web application that lets users upload CSV files, ask questions in plain English, and receive instant {bold & highlight}AI-generated SQL queries{bold & highlight}, interactive charts, and data insights.
projects.longDescription: {bold}INTELLI Query{bold} is a zero-dependency, self-contained BI dashboard built with vanilla JavaScript and Node.js. It leverages {bold}Google Gemini{bold} to{bold & highlight} translate natural language questions into SQL{bold & highlight}, executing queries locally using an in-process WebAssembly database (sql.js). Users can preview schemas, run queries, and visualize results instantly using dynamic Chart.js dashboards, making data analysis intuitive and secure.

projects.summary: {bold & highlight}MedLens{bold & highlight} transforms unstructured medical reports into grounded, validated patient records with source traceability and safety.
projects.description: {bold & highlight}MedLens{bold & highlight} transforms unstructured medical reports into grounded, validated patient records with source traceability and safety.
projects.longDescription: {bold & highlight}MedLens{bold & highlight} is an{bold & highlight} AI clinical intelligence platform{bold & highlight} that transforms fragmented medical documents into structured, FHIR-compliant records. projects.title: AI Hiring Assistant
projects.summary: {bold}AI Hiring Assistant{bold} is a full-stack web application that uses OCR to extract text from candidate certificates and leverages LLaMA 3.1 to{bold & highlight} perform fraud analysis and ranking{bold & highlight}.
projects.description: {bold}AI Hiring Assistant{bold} is a full-stack web application that uses OCR to extract text from candidate certificates and leverages LLaMA 3.1 to{bold & highlight} perform fraud analysis and ranking{bold & highlight}.
projects.longDescription: {bold}AI Hiring Assistant{bold} is a modular full-stack application designed to streamline recruiting. The backend is built with Node.js and Express, while the frontend is constructed using clean, responsive HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript. The system utilizes Tesseract.js to extract text from candidate certificates, executes simulated academic institution validation, and leverages LLaMA 3.1 via the Featherless API to analyze fraud risk. Finally, a{bold & highlight} ranking service computes score metrics to provide automated, reliable recommendations for hiring teams.{bold & highlight}

projects.description: {bold}VaultFlow{bold} is a local Android{bold & highlight} personal finance application{bold & highlight} built using Jetpack Compose. The app features secure offline database storage, receipt scanning, and smart budgeting insights powered by the Gemini API.
projects.longDescription: {bold}VaultFlow{bold} is a comprehensive {bold & highlight}personal finance manager{bold & highlight} designed for Android with privacy and offline capabilities at its core. {highlight}Developed in Kotlin using Jetpack Compose{highlight}, the application allows users to manage multiple bank accounts, track recurring transactions, monitor savings goals, and track debts. The app integrates Google ML Kit for scanning receipts via OCR and leverages the Gemini API to deliver personalized financial insights directly on the device. All data is stored locally in a Room database, ensuring complete user privacy.

blogs.title: My Journey from Minecraft Mods in 8th Class to Full-Stack Development
blogs.snippet: How curious experimentation with Minecraft textures and small game tweaks ignited a lifelong passion for computer science and web engineering.
blogs.content:
Back in 8th class, I was fascinated by Minecraft. What started as simple curiosity about texture packs and game modifications quickly sparked a deep interest in how software works behind the scenes.

### From Modding to Programming

Tinkering with configuration files and basic code logic taught me problem-solving early on. Eventually, that curiosity led me to explore fundamental programming languages like C, Java, and Python.

### Stepping Into Web Development

When I entered Computer Science Engineering at MVSR Engineering College, I turned that interest towards full-stack web development. Learning React, Node.js, Express, and databases (MySQL & MongoDB) allowed me to build functional applications that solve real student and campus needs.

Never underestimate small sparks of curiosity—they often lead to your greatest skills.

blogs.title: Designing Eye-Catching College Event Posters with Canva & AI Tools
blogs.snippet: Practical tips for engineering students on blending AI design tools, Canva, and clean typography to create striking event posters.
blogs.content:
As a Computer Science student who loves creative design, I often design posters for MVSR college events and NSS activities.

### Key Principles for Event Posters:

1. **Hierarchy First**: Make the event name and key date/time immediately readable from a distance.
2. **Color Contrast**: Use clean dark backgrounds paired with sharp white and vibrant accent colors.
3. **AI Assistance**: Utilize AI tools like ChatGPT or Gemini to brainstorm catchy taglines, then use Canva or Photoshop for final composition.

Combining tech with creative design allows engineering projects and campus events to stand out!

blogs.title: Building Practical Web Apps with React, Express, and MongoDB
blogs.snippet: A student developer guide on setting up full-stack MERN architecture for campus projects and portfolio applications.
blogs.content:
Building web applications as a student is one of the best ways to solidify classroom computer science concepts.

### Why MERN Stack Works Well:

* **JavaScript Everywhere**: Write frontend React components and backend Node/Express routes in the same language.
* **Flexible Schemas**: MongoDB allows rapid iteration when adding new features.
* **Tailwind CSS Utility Styling**: Achieve clean Vercel/Apple inspired layouts with minimal custom CSS overhead.

Keep building real projects—hands-on practice beats theoretical reading every time!
